Frequency the Elevation Recurs in Percent
1. These graphs show data similar to those on plate IV-1 in that they refer to the elevations that will be maintained in the two reservoirs under the two conditions of present and proposed (defined as Study A and Study B on plate IV-1). However, where the previous plate showed the time interval in years, this plate shows the percent of time the reservoirs will be at or above any particular elevation.
2. Explanation of Amistad Reservoir Graph. In general, the pool will be lower under the proposed condition. For example, under present conditions, the water surface will be at or above elevation 1101.1 for 50 percent of the time. And for the proposed condition, the water surface elevation will be at or above 1100.3 for 50 percent of the time. Under present conditions the pool will be in flood stage (i.e., above elevation 1117.0) about 26 percent of the time. Under proposed conditions it would be in flood stage about 24 percent of the time.
3. Explanation of Falcon Reservoir Graph. In general, the pool will be higher under the proposed condition. For example, under present conditions, the pool will be at elevation 262.5 for 50 percent of the time, and under the proposed condition the pool will be at elevation 264.6 for 50 percent of the time. Also, the reservoir will be in flood stage (i.e., above elevation 301.1) only about 2 percent of the time whether or not the power facilities are added at Amistad Reservoir.
4. Summary of Graphs on Plate IV-2. The pool at Amistad Reservoir will be lower on average with very little change in the flood control pool. The pool at Falcon Reservoir will be higher on average with no significant change in the flood control pool.
